"gui/ImageProcTest/Services/AppSettingsService.cs": "using System.IO;\nusing System.Text.Json;\nusing ImageProcTest.Models;\n\nnamespace ImageProcTest.Services;\n\n/// <summary>\n/// What a load The failure had no place to\n/// live in the old signature; this record is that place.</para>\n/// </summary>\n/// <param name=\"Settings\">The settings to run with \u2014 the stored ones, or defaults when they could not be read.</param>\n/// <param name=\"PreservedOriginalPath\">\n/// Where the user's original settings are kept, or null when the file loaded (or when there was no\n/// file, or when preserving it failed).\n/// </param>\n/// <param name=\"PreservedIsFromAnEarlierFailure\">\n/// True when this path was rescued by an EARLIER failed read rather than this one \u2014 see\n/// <see cref=\"AppSettingsService.Load\"/> for why the earlier rescue is the valuable one.\n/// </param>\npublic sealed record SettingsLoadResult(\n    AppSettings Settings,\n    string? PreservedOriginalPath,\n    bool PreservedIsFromAnEarlierFailure = false)\n{\n    /// <summary>True when the stored file existed but could not be read.</summary>\n    public bool FailedToRead => PreservedOriginalPath is not null;\n}\n\npublic sealed class AppSettingsService\n{\n    private readonly JsonSerializerOptions _serializerOptions = new()\n    {\n        WriteIndented = true\n    };\n\n    public AppSettingsService(string? filePath = null)\n    {\n        FilePath = filePath ?? This happens once, at the\n    /// failed read \u2014 it is not a rolling backup of good files.</para>\n    ///\n    /// <para><b>An existing rescue is never replaced (#173, GUI-C-120).</b> The file rescued at the\n    /// FIRST failure is the user's real settings; by the time a second failure happens this path has\n    /// been rewritten from defaults (GUI-C-118 measured the next Save putting 1482 bytes over it), so\n    /// a later rescue holds something closer to defaults than to what the user had. Keeping the newest\n    /// would discard exactly the thing worth keeping, and keeping both would accumulate files with\n    /// nobody to remove them. So the count stays at one, and that one is the earliest.</para>\n    ///\n    /// <para>Still no exception leaves this method. An app that dies at startup over a settings file is\n    /// worse than one that starts at defaults: people come here to look at images.</para>\n    /// </summary>\n    public SettingsLoadResult Load()\n    {\n        if (!File.Exists(FilePath))\n        {\n            return new SettingsLoadResult(new AppSettings(), null);\n        }\n\n        try\n        {\n            var json = File.ReadAllText(FilePath);\n            var settings = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<AppSettings>(json, _serializerOptions);\n            if (settings is not null)\n            {\n                // GUI-C-234c (Codex #181 finding 1): a stored \"preprocessInChain\": false is kept - the loader cannot tell the old default from a choice - and the operator is told once.\n                // GUI-C-234d (Codex #182): only an OFF stored by an EARLIER build (no schema version, or a lower one) is the old default's; a current-version file's OFF is the operator's choice. The flag is stored\n                // until acknowledged, so it is kept (not recomputed away) once a later save has stamped the file with the current version.\n                if (!settings.PreprocessOffNoticeUnacknowledged && StoresPreprocessOffFromAnEarlierBuild(json))\n                {\n                    settings.PreprocessOffNoticeUnacknowledged = true;\n                }\n                return new SettingsLoadResult(settings, null);\n            }\n        }\n        catch\n        {\n            // Fall through to preservation. The reason is not reported: every reason has the same\n            // consequence for the user, and the file itself is kept so the detail is not lost.\n        }\n\n        var earlier = ExistingRescue();\n        if (earlier is not null)\n        {\n            // Leave both this unreadable file and the earlier rescue where they are. The caller says\n            // where the earlier one is, so the user can still find what they had.\n            return new SettingsLoadResult(new AppSettings(), earlier, PreservedIsFromAnEarlierFailure: true);\n        }\n\n        var rescued = PreserveUnreadable();\n        var defaults = new AppSettings();\n\n        if (rescued is not null)\n        {\n            // The original is safe, so the path it left empty is filled with defaults and the next\n            // launch is quiet (#173, GUI-C-121). Leaving it unreadable would repeat this warning on\n            // every start, and a warning that always appears is one nobody reads.\n            //\n            // Only a run that actually rescued may do this. When the rescue failed the file below is\n            // still the user's only copy, so it is left exactly as it is \u2014 writing defaults over it\n            // would undo what GUI-C-119 set out to keep.\n            TryWriteDefaults(defaults);\n        }\n\n        return new SettingsLoadResult(defaults, rescued);\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>\n    /// Moves the unreadable file aside and returns its new path, or null when even that failed.\n    ///\n    /// <para>A failure here must not stop the app starting, so it is swallowed like the read failure \u2014\n    /// but it returns null rather than a path, so the caller never tells the user the original is\n    /// somewhere it is not.</para>\n    /// </summary>\n    private static bool StoresPreprocessOffFromAnEarlierBuild(string json)\n    {\n        try\n        {\n            using var document = JsonDocument.Parse(json);\n            var root = document.RootElement;\n            if (root.ValueKind != JsonValueKind.Object\n                || !root.TryGetProperty(\"preprocessInChain\", out var value)\n                || value.ValueKind != JsonValueKind.False)\n            {\n                return false;\n            }\n\n            var current = root.TryGetProperty(\"settingsSchemaVersion\", out var version)\n                && version.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Number\n                && version.TryGetInt32(out var number)\n                && number >= AppSettings.CurrentSchemaVersion;\n            return !current;\n        }\n        catch (JsonException)\n        {\n            return false;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>\n    /// The rescue an earlier failed read left behind, or null when there is none.\n    ///\n    /// <para>The earliest is returned when several exist \u2014 a tree carrying more than one predates this\n    /// rule, and the earliest is still the one closest to what the user had. The names are timestamped\n    /// in a sortable format, so ordinal order is chronological order.</para>\n    /// </summary>\n    private string? ExistingRescue()\n    {\n        try\n        {\n            var directory = Path.GetDirectoryName(FilePath);\n            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(directory)) return null;\n\n            return Directory\n                .GetFiles(directory, Path.GetFileName(FilePath) + \".unreadable-*\")\n                .OrderBy(path => path, StringComparer.Ordinal)\n                .FirstOrDefault();\n        }\n        catch\n        {\n            return null;\n        }\n    }\n\n    private string? Nothing else is changed: every answer is the Mock's.\n/// </summary>\ninternal class ScenarioBackend : IXpeBackend\n{\n    private readonly IXpeBackend _inner = new MockXpeBackend(new RawImageLoader(), \"xpe_common.dll\", false, \"xpe_display.dll\", false);\n\n    public int LoadCalls;\n    public int PresetCalls;\n    public int ChainCalls;\n    public int ApplyCalls;\n\n    /// <summary>How many chain calls requested the AI stage, and for each call, in order, whether it did (GUI-C-191).</summary>\n    public int AiCalls;\n\n    public readonly System.Collections.Concurrent.ConcurrentQueue<bool> AiStageRequestedPerCall = new();\n\n    /// <summary>The 1-based RunChain call that waits for <see cref=\"ChainRelease\"/> (0: none).</summary>\n    public int BlockChainCall;\n\n    /// <summary>The held call throws when released (else it carries on and succeeds).</summary>\n    public bool ThrowAfterRelease;\n\n    public readonly ManualResetEventSlim ChainBlocked = new();\n    public readonly ManualResetEventSlim ChainRelease = new();\n\n    /// <summary>When set, Shutdown waits for it: the transition stays running until the scenario lets it end.</summary>\n    public ManualResetEventSlim? ShutdownMayEnd;\n\n    public virtual ChainResult RunChain(LoadedImageFrame rawFrame, IReadOnlyList<StageRequest> stages, AppSettings settings)\n    {\n        var call = Interlocked.Increment(ref ChainCalls);\n        var requestsAi = stages.Any(stage => stage.StageId == StageIds.AiBoneSuppression && stage.Enabled);\n        AiStageRequestedPerCall.Enqueue(requestsAi);\n        if (requestsAi)\n        {\n            Interlocked.Increment(ref AiCalls);\n        }\n\n        if (call == BlockChainCall)\n        {\n            ChainBlocked.Set();\n            if (!ChainRelease.Wait(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30)))\n            {\n                throw new TimeoutException(\"the scenario never released the held chain call\");\n            }\n\n            if (ThrowAfterRelease)\n            {\n                throw new InvalidOperationException(\"scripted failure of the held chain call\");\n            }\n        }\n\n        return _inner.RunChain(rawFrame, stages, settings);\n    }\n\n    public virtual LoadedImageFrame LoadRawImage(string path, AppSettings settings)\n    {\n        Interlocked.Increment(ref LoadCalls);\n        return _inner.LoadRawImage(path, settings);\n    }\n\n    public VoiPreset CreateVoiPreset(XpeBodyPartEnum bodyPart)\n    {\n        Interlocked.Increment(ref PresetCalls);\n        return _inner.CreateVoiPreset(bodyPart);\n    }\n\n    public virtual LoadedImageFrame ApplyDisplayPipeline(LoadedImageFrame rawFrame, ushort[] displayInput, AppSettings settings)\n    {\n        Interlocked.Increment(ref ApplyCalls);\n        return _inner.ApplyDisplayPipeline(rawFrame, displayInput, settings);\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>GUI-C-234c: the display call over a chain run's result (the one the view model makes); the default is the 16-bit call.</summary>\n    public virtual LoadedImageFrame ApplyDisplayPipeline(LoadedImageFrame rawFrame, ChainResult chain, AppSettings settings) =>\n        ApplyDisplayPipeline(rawFrame, chain.DisplayInput, settings);\n\n    public void Shutdown()\n    {\n        ShutdownMayEnd?.Wait(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30));\n        _inner.Shutdown();\n    }\n\n    public virtual BackendRuntimeInfo Initialize(AppSettings settings) => _inner.Initialize(settings);\n\n    public string GetVersion() => _inner.GetVersion();\n\n    public bool SupportsPreprocessing => _inner.SupportsPreprocessing;\n\n    public string GetDisplayVersion() => _inner.GetDisplayVersion();\n\n    public TelemetrySnapshot GetTelemetrySince(int logsSeen, int alertsSeen) => _inner.GetTelemetrySince(logsSeen, alertsSeen);\n\n    public virtual BackendRuntimeInfo GetRuntimeInfo() => _inner.GetRuntimeInfo();\n}\n\n/// <summary>GUI-C-233k: a scripted backend whose preprocess stage reports the status the scenario chooses (the Mock never runs one); The runner has no window, so the wait for ticks is scripted through CompositionTicksOverride; the real wait is exercised directly.\n\n    private const string TimingPrefix = \"open-to-2nd-tick (proxy) #\";\n\n    private static async Task TheFrameTimingOfAnOpen_IsNeverWrittenLate_AndSaysWhenItTimedOut_AndLeavesNoSubscription(string rawPath, int width, int height)\n    {\n        _scenario = \"10 frame timing of an open\";\n\n        // control: an undisturbed open writes its line (so the absence checks below are not an artifact of a wait that never publishes)\n        var directory =       {\n            Directory.Delete(directory, recursive: true);\n        }\n\n        // the REAL wait: whichever way it ends - ticks, timeout, cancellation - the subscription is gone. (No window here, so a tick may never come; the outcome is printed, the count is what is checked.)\n        Check(MainWindowViewModel.ActiveCompositionSubscriptions == 0, $\"a subscription was already held before the check ({MainWindowViewModel.ActiveCompositionSubscriptions})\");\n        // GUI-C-241: the time-out path is made deterministic by asking for ticks that cannot come (int.MaxValue of them), so the limit is the only way out; and no count is asserted WHILE this wait runs:\n        // its limit is short, and a loaded runner can stall this thread for longer than the limit between the call and the check (measured: 2 of 12 instances run in parallel failed with\n        // \"a running wait holds 0 subscriptions\"). The pedestal is\n// what the offset map should recover.\nstd::vector<std::vector<uint16_t>> makeDarkFrames(const Options& opt, int count) {\n    std::mt19937 gen(opt.seed);\n    std::normal_distribution<double> noise(0.0, 8.0);\n    const size_t n = static_cast<size_t>(opt.width) * opt.height;\n\n    std::vector<std::vector<uint16_t>> frames;\n    for (int f = 0; f < count; ++f) {\n        std::vector<uint16_t> px(n);\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n            const double v = 300.0 + noise(gen);\n            px[i] = static_cast<uint16_t>(v < 0.0 ? 0.0 : (v > 65535.0 ? 65535.0 : v));\n        }\n        frames.push_back(std::move(px));\n    }\n    return frames;\n}\n\n// Flat frames: a smooth left-to-right sensitivity ramp on the pedestal, so the\n// normalised gain map has structure rather than being uniformly 1.0.\n//\n// `exposure` scales the signal (1.0 is the original level) and `seedOffset`\n// picks a distinct noise stream. Both default to the pre-QA-A-136 values, so\n// makeFlatFrames(opt, n) produces exactly what it always did -- the scalar\n// fixture stays byte-identical.\nstd::vector<std::vector<uint16_t>> makeFlatFrames(const Options& opt, int count,\n                                                  double exposure = 1.0,\n                                                  uint32_t seedOffset = 1u) {\n    std::mt19937 gen(opt.seed + seedOffset);\n    std::normal_distribution<double> noise(0.0, 20.0);\n    const size_t n = static_cast<size_t>(opt.width) * opt.height;\n\n    std::vector<std::vector<uint16_t>> frames;\n    for (int f = 0; f < count; ++f) {\n        std::vector<uint16_t> px(n);\n        for (uint32_t y = 0; y < opt.height; ++y) {\n            for (uint32_t x = 0; x < opt.width; ++x) {\n                // +-10% sensitivity across the width, centred on 1.0\n                const double sensitivity =\n                    0.9 + 0.2 * (static_cast<double>(x) / (opt.width - 1u ? opt.width - 1u : 1u));\n                const double v = 300.0 + 20000.0 * exposure * sensitivity + noise(gen);\n                px[static_cast<size_t>(y) * opt.width + x] =\n                    static_cast<uint16_t>(v < 0.0 ? 0.0 : (v > 65535.0 ? 65535.0 : v));\n            }\n        }\n        frames.push_back(std::move(px));\n    }\n    return frames;\n}\n\n// A handful of defects at fixed coordinates: two dead (stuck low) and two hot\n// (stuck high), placed so they survive any reasonable detector threshold.\nstruct DefectSpot { uint32_t x, y; bool hot; };\n\nstd::vector<DefectSpot> defectSpots(const Options& opt) {\n    const uint32_t w = opt.width, h = opt.height;\n    return {\n        {w / 4u,       h / 4u,       false},\n        {w / 2u,       h / 2u,       true},\n        {3u * w / 4u,  h / 3u,       true},\n        {w / 3u,       3u * h / 4u,  false},\n    };\n}\n\nvoid injectDefects(std::vector<uint16_t>& frame, const Options& opt) {\n    for (const auto& d : defectSpots(opt)) {\n        frame[static_cast<size_t>(d.y) * opt.width + d.x] = d.hot ? 65535u : 0u;\n    }\n}\n\n/* ------------------------------------------------------- frames mode (QA-A-250) */\n\nconstexpr size_t kMinDarkFrames       = 5;      // offset map, gain dark reference, defect map (XpeBpmConfig.min_frames_dark)\nconstexpr size_t kMinGainFrames       = 5;      // SRS-CALIB-FUNC-024, standard tier (5-10 frames)\nconstexpr size_t kMinBrightForBpm     = 10;     // XpeBpmConfig.min_frames_bright\nconstexpr double kSaturatedShareLimit = 0.001;  // a frame with more than 0.1 % of its pixels at 65535 is saturated, not defective\n// QA-A-250b: bright frames of the GAIN map must come from one dose. Basis (evidence 10_dose_spread_basis.txt, the 20 cyan_test bright frames, offset level =\n// mean of the eight generation darks): inside one dose level the largest max/min of the offset-subtracted frame mean is 1.0712 (Bright_17..19, a first-frame\n// step); between two dose levels the smallest step is 1.5593, and no adjacent ratio lies between the two. 1.25 sits between them (1.167 times above the largest\n// spread inside a level, 1.247 times below the smallest step between levels). One data set; a panel whose dose steps are smaller than 25 % would pass mixed.\nconstexpr double kGainDoseRatioLimit  = 1.25;\n\nstruct InputFrame {\n    std::string           role;\n    std::string           path;\n    std::vector<uint16_t> px;\n    std::string           sha;\n    double                mean{0.0};\n};\n\nstd::string jsonText(const std::string& text) {\n    std::string out;\n    for (char c : text) {\n        if (c == '\"' || c == '\\\\') out.push_back('\\\\');\n        out.push_back(c);\n    }\n    return out;\n}\n\nstd::string fixed(double v, int digits) {\n    char buf[64];\n    std::snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, \"%.*f\", digits, v);\n    return buf;\n}\n\n/** One path per line; '#' and empty lines are skipped; a relative path is relative to the list file. */\nbool readList(const std::string& listPath, std::vector<std::string>* out) {\n    std::ifstream f(listPath);\n    if (!f) {\n        std::fprintf(stderr, \"cannot open list %s\\n\", listPath.c_str());\n        return false;\n    }\n    const fs::path base = fs::path(listPath).parent_path();\n    std::string line;\n    while (std::getline(f, line)) {\n        while (!line.empty() && (line.back() == '\\r' || line.back() == ' ' || line.back() == '\\t')) line.pop_back();\n        size_t b = 0;\n        while (b < line.size() && (line[b] == ' ' || line[b] == '\\t')) ++b;\n        line.erase(0, b);\n        if (line.empty() || line[0] == '#') continue;\n        const fs::path p(line);\n        out->push_back((p.is_absolute() ? p : base / p).generic_string());\n    }\n    return true;\n}\n\n/** Reads every frame, refusing a wrong size (readFrame16) and a saturated frame. Returns 0, 9 or 11. */\nint loadFrames(const std::vector<std::string>& paths, const char* role, size_t pixelCount, std::vector<InputFrame>* out) {\n    for (const std::string& p : paths) {\n        InputFrame fr;\n        fr.role = role;\n        fr.path = p;\n        if (!readFrame16(p, pixelCount, &fr.px)) return 9;\n        uint64_t sum = 0;\n        size_t saturated = 0;\n        for (uint16_t v : fr.px) {\n            sum += v;\n            if (v == 65535u) ++saturated;\n        }\n        fr.mean = static_cast<double>(sum) / static_cast<double>(pixelCount);\n        const double share = static_cast<double>(saturated) / static_cast<double>(pixelCount);\n        if (share > kSaturatedShareLimit) {\n            std::fprintf(stderr, \"%s: %.4f %% of the pixels are at 65535 (limit %.2f %%): a saturated frame cannot be averaged into a calibration map\\n\", p.c_str(),\n                         share * 100.0, kSaturatedShareLimit * 100.0);\n            return 11;\n        }\n        fr.sha = sha256Hex(p);\n        out->push_back(std::move(fr));\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n\n/** A defect map from someone else: uint8 (N bytes) or uint16 (2N bytes); flags[i] = 1 when the value is not zero. */\nbool readReferenceMask(const std::string& path, size_t pixelCount, std::vector<uint8_t>* flags) {\n    std::error_code ec;\n    const auto size = fs::file_size(path, ec);\n    if (ec) {\n        std::fprintf(stderr, \"cannot open %s\\n\", path.c_str());\n        return false;\n    }\n    if (size != pixelCount && size != pixelCount * 2) {\n        std::fprintf(stderr, \"%s is %llu bytes, expected %zu (uint8) or %zu (uint16) for width x height\\n\", path.c_str(), static_cast<unsigned long long>(size), pixelCount,\n                     pixelCount * 2);\n        return false;\n    }\n    std::vector<uint8_t> bytes;\n    if (!readExact(path, static_cast<size_t>(size), &bytes)) return false;\n    flags->assign(pixelCount, 0u);\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < pixelCount; ++i) {\n        (*flags)[i] = (size == pixelCount) ? (bytes[i] != 0u) : ((bytes[2 * i] | bytes[2 * i + 1]) != 0u);\n    }\n    return true;\n}\n\nstd::vector<XpeImageBuffer> u16Buffers(std::vector<InputFrame>& frames, uint32_t w, uint32_t h) {\n    std::vector<XpeImageBuffer> bufs;\n    for (auto& f : frames) bufs.push_back(u16Buffer(f.px, w, h));\n    return bufs;\n}\n\nstd::vector<XpeImageBuffer> u16BuffersOf(const std::vector<InputFrame*>& frames, uint32_t w, uint32_t h) {\n    std::vector<XpeImageBuffer> bufs;\n    for (InputFrame* f : frames) bufs.push_back(u16Buffer(f->px, w, h));\n    return bufs;\n}\n\n/**\n * The signal of a bright frame as the gain generator forms it: the mean over the pixels of max(0, frame - dark reference). @p ref empty means no subtraction.\n */\ndouble gainSignalMean(const std::vector<uint16_t>& frame, const std::vector<uint16_t>& ref) {\n    double sum = 0.0;\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < frame.size(); ++i) {\n        const double corrected = static_cast<double>(frame[i]) - (ref.empty() ? 0.0 : static_cast<double>(ref[i]));\n        if (corrected > 0.0) sum += corrected;\n    }\n    return sum / static_cast<double>(frame.size());\n}\n\n/**\n * The gain map averages its bright frames, so they must come from one dose. The dose is judged on the signal the generator will see (gainSignalMean with\n * the reference the generator will get), so the check and the generator cannot disagree. Returns 0 and the max/min ratio, or 12 with the reason on stderr.\n */\nint checkSingleDose(const std::vector<InputFrame>& brights, const std::vector<uint16_t>& ref, const std::string& refLabel, double* ratio) {\n    const InputFrame* lo = nullptr;\n    const InputFrame* hi = nullptr;\n    double loSig = 0.0, hiSig = 0.0;\n    for (const auto& b : brights) {\n        const double sig = gainSignalMean(b.px, ref);\n        if (sig <= 0.0) {\n            std::fprintf(stderr, \"%s: no signal is left after subtracting the gain dark reference (%s): mean of max(0, frame - reference) is %.3f; not a bright frame for this reference\\n\",\n                         b.path.c_str(), refLabel.c_str(), sig);\n            return 12;\n        }\n        if (!lo || sig < loSig) { lo = &b; loSig = sig; }\n        if (!hi || sig > hiSig) { hi = &b; hiSig = sig; }\n    }\n    *ratio = hiSig / loSig;\n    if (*ratio > kGainDoseRatioLimit) {\n        std::fprintf(stderr,\n                     \"bright frames for the gain map span more than one dose: gain signal (mean of max(0, frame - gain dark reference %s)) from %.1f (%s) to %.1f (%s), ratio %.3f, limit %.2f. The gain \"\n                     \"generator averages its frames and assumes one dose; give frames of one dose with --bright (frames of several doses may go to the defect map with --bpm-bright)\\n\",\n                     refLabel.c_str(), loSig, lo->path.c_str(), hiSig, hi->path.c_str(), *ratio, kGainDoseRatioLimit);\n        return 12;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n\n// QA-A-250c: the same file twice in one role. A path duplicate is the same normalized path or the same file (fs::equivalent: links, case, ..), a content\n// duplicate the same sha-256. The first would be counted twice toward the frame minimum and averaged twice; a duplicate is refused (exit 13), not skipped.\nint rejectPathDuplicates(const std::vector<std::string>& paths, const char* role) {\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < paths.size(); ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = i + 1; j < paths.size(); ++j) {\n            std::error_code ec;\n            const bool same = fs::path(paths[i]).lexically_normal() == fs::path(paths[j]).lexically_normal() || fs::equivalent(paths[i], paths[j], ec);\n            if (same) {\n                std::fprintf(stderr, \"duplicate %s frame: '%s' and '%s' are the same file; a frame is given once per role\\n\", role, paths[i].c_str(), paths[j].c_str());\n                return 13;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n\nint rejectContentDuplicates(const std::vector<const InputFrame*>& frames, const char* role) {\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < frames.size(); ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = i + 1; j < frames.size(); ++j) {\n            if (frames[i]->sha == frames[j]->sha) {\n                std::fprintf(stderr, \"duplicate %s frame: '%s' and '%s' have the same content (sha-256 %s); a frame is given once per role\\n\", role, frames[i]->path.c_str(),\n                             frames[j]->path.c_str(), frames[i]->sha.c_str());\n                return 13;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n\n// Test seam: XPE_FIXTURE_GEN_FAIL=<stage> forces that stage to fail (gain, bpm, manifest, commit) so the rollback paths can be exercised.\nbool forcedFailure(const char* stage) {\n#ifdef _WIN32\n    char* v = nullptr;\n    size_t len = 0;\n    const bool hit = _dupenv_s(&v, &len, \"XPE_FIXTURE_GEN_FAIL\") == 0 && v != nullptr && std::strcmp(v, stage) == 0;\n    std::free(v);\n    return hit;\n#else\n    const char* v = std::getenv(\"XPE_FIXTURE_GEN_FAIL\");\n    return v != nullptr && std::strcmp(v, stage) == 0;\n#endif\n}\n\n// The work directory is a sibling of --out with a name of this run alone (<out>.building-<pid>-<ms>), so a leftover of a killed run or a run on the same\n// --out at the same time never shares it. It is created empty and is never cleaned up on behalf of another run. It is removed in every case (after a\n// successful publish it no longer exists), together with the parent directories this run had to create.\nstruct WorkDir {\n    fs::path path, firstExisting;\n    bool     created{false};\n    explicit WorkDir(const fs::path& out) {\n        fs::path abs = fs::absolute(out).lexically_normal();\n        if (abs.filename().empty()) abs = abs.parent_path();\n        const long long ms = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(std::chrono::system_clock::now().time_since_epoch()).count();\n        path = abs.parent_path() / (abs.filename().string() + \".building-\" + std::to_string(XPE_GETPID()) + \"-\" + std::to_string(ms));\n        firstExisting = abs;\n        std::error_code ec;\n        while (!firstExisting.empty() && !fs::exists(firstExisting, ec) && firstExisting != firstExisting.parent_path()) firstExisting = firstExisting.parent_path();\n        fs::create_directories(path.parent_path(), ec);\n        created = fs::create_directory(path, ec);   // false when the name is taken: never adopt a directory that is not ours\n    }\n    bool ok() const { return created; }\n    ~WorkDir() {\n        std::error_code ec;\n        if (created) fs::remove_all(path, ec);\n        for (fs::path d = path.parent_path(); !d.empty() && d != firstExisting && d != d.parent_path(); d = d.parent_path()) fs::remove(d, ec);   // only if empty\n    }\n};\n\n// QA-A-250d: publishes the finished set with one directory rename onto --out. A failed rename is a failure (exit 8), never reported as success.\nint publishSet(const fs::path& work, const fs::path& out) {\n    std::error_code ec;\n    const bool wasEmptyDir = fs::is_directory(out, ec);\n    if (wasEmptyDir) {\n        fs::remove(out, ec);   // removes an empty directory only\n        if (ec) {\n            std::fprintf(stderr, \"cannot publish into %s: %s\\n\", out.string().c_str(), ec.message().c_str());\n            return 8;\n        }\n    }\n    if (forcedFailure(\"commit\")) ec = std::make_error_code(std::errc::io_error);\n    else fs::rename(work, out, ec);\n    if (ec) {\n        if (wasEmptyDir) fs::create_directory(out, ec);\n        std::fprintf(stderr, \"publishing the finished set to %s failed; nothing was published\\n\", out.string().c_str());\n        return 8;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n\nint runFramesMode(const Options& opt) {\n    const fs::path out(opt.outDir);\n    const size_t pixelCount = static_cast<size_t>(opt.width) * opt.height;\n\n    std::vector<std::string> darkPaths = opt.darkFiles, brightPaths = opt.brightFiles;\n    if (!opt.darkList.empty() && !readList(opt.darkList, &darkPaths)) return 9;\n    if (!opt.brightList.empty() && !readList(opt.brightList, &brightPaths)) return 9;\n    std::vector<std::string> bpmPaths = opt.bpmBrightFiles;\n    if (!opt.bpmBrightList.empty() && !readList(opt.bpmBrightList, &bpmPaths)) return 9;\n    const bool separateBpm = !bpmPaths.empty();\n\n    {\n        std::error_code ec;\n        if (fs::exists(out, ec)) {\n            if (!fs::is_directory(out, ec)) {\n                std::fprintf(stderr, \"cannot create output directory: %s exists and is not a directory\\n\", opt.outDir.c_str());\n                return 3;\n            }\n            if (!fs::is_empty(out, ec)) {\n                std::fprintf(stderr, \"output directory %s is not empty: nothing was written. The subscription to <c>CompositionTarget.Rendering</c> is taken\n    /// and released HERE and nowhere else, and it is released in a <c>finally</c>: whichever way the wait ends, no handler is left behind (a static event keeps every handler - and the closure it holds - alive).\n    /// WPF can raise <c>Rendering</c> more than once for one frame; a frame is told by its <c>RenderingTime</c>, so one frame counts once.\n    /// </summary>\n    internal static async Task<CompositionWait> WaitForCompositionTicksAsync(int ticks, TimeSpan limit, CancellationToken cancel)\n    {\n        var done = new TaskCompletionSource<CompositionWait>(TaskCreationOptions.RunContinuationsAsynchronously);\n        var seen = 0;\n        TimeSpan? lastFrame = null;\n        EventHandler handler = (_, e) =>\n        {\n            var frame = (e as System.Windows.Media.RenderingEventArgs)?.RenderingTime;\n            if (frame is not null && frame == lastFrame)\n            {\n                return;\n            }\n\n            lastFrame = frame;\n            if (++seen >= ticks)\n            {\n                done.TrySetResult(CompositionWait.Ticked);\n            }\n        };\n\n        using var timeout = new CancellationTokenSource(limit);\n        using var onTimeout = timeout.Token.Register(() => done.TrySetResult(CompositionWait.TimedOut));\n        using var onCancel = cancel.Register(() => done.TrySetResult(CompositionWait.Cancelled));\n        try\n        {\n            Interlocked.Increment(ref ActiveCompositionSubscriptions);\n            System.Windows.Media.CompositionTarget.Rendering += handler;\n            return await done.Task;\n        }\n        finally\n        {\n            System.Windows.Media.CompositionTarget.Rendering -= handler;\n            Interlocked.Decrement(ref ActiveCompositionSubscriptions);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>Called when the backend is going away (the window is closing): a wait still running ends as cancelled and writes nothing.</summary>\n    private void CancelFrameTiming()\n    {\n        var old = Interlocked.Exchange(ref _frameTimingLifetime, new CancellationTokenSource());\n        old.Cancel();\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>\n    /// Waits for the second composition tick after <paramref name=\"shown\"/> was handed to the viewport and writes the line - unless, when the wait ends, it no longer describes what is on screen: a newer\n    /// open began (<paramref name=\"generation\"/> is no longer the current one) or another picture replaced <paramref name=\"shown\"/>. Chosen because it both crosses the\n        // ABI and returns something checkable \u2014 a code AND a non-null pointer.\n        try\n        {\n            var code = XpeCommonNative.xpe_alloc_image(16, 16, XpePixelFormatNative.UInt16, out var buffer);\n            if (code != 0)\n            {\n                failed++;\n                outcomes.Add($\"xpe_alloc_image -> code {code} (expected 0)\");\n            }\n            else if (buffer.Data == IntPtr.Zero)\n            {\n                failed++;\n                outcomes.Add(\"xpe_alloc_image -> code 0 but a null data pointer\");\n                XpeCommonNative.xpe_free_image(ref buffer);\n            }\n            else\n            {\n                var freeCode = XpeCommonNative.xpe_free_image(ref buffer);\n                if (freeCode != 0)\n                {\n                    failed++;\n                    outcomes.Add($\"xpe_free_image -> code {freeCode} (expected 0)\");\n                }\n                else\n                {\n                    outcomes.Add(\"xpe_alloc_image/xpe_free_image -> ok\");\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        catch (Exception ex)\n        {\n            failed++;\n            outcomes.Add($\"xpe_alloc_image threw {ex.GetType().Name}: {ex.Message}\");\n        }\n\n        // Probe 2: the (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(version) || version == \"unknown\")\n            {\n                failed++;\n                outcomes.Add($\"xpe_display_version -> '{version}'\");\n            }\n            else\n            {\n                outcomes.Add($\"xpe_display_version -> '{version}'\");\n            }\n        }\n        catch (Exception ex)\n        {\n            failed++;\n            outcomes.Add($\"xpe_display_version threw {ex.GetType().Name}: {ex.Message}\");\n        }\n\n        // Probe 3: the alert queue answers. A negative count would mean the call crossed but the\n        // contract did not hold, which is a different failure from the library being absent.\n        try\n        {\n            var count = XpeCommonNative.xpe_get_pending_alert_count();\n            if (count < 0)\n            {\n                failed++;\n                outcomes.Add($\"xpe_get_pending_alert_count -> {count} (expected >= 0)\");\n            }\n            else\n            {\n                outcomes.Add($\"xpe_get_pending_alert_count -> {count}\");\n            }\n        }\n        catch (Exception ex)\n        {\n            failed++;\n            outcomes.Add($\"xpe_get_pending_alert_count threw {ex.GetType().Name}: {ex.Message}\");\n        }\n\n        var total = outcomes.Count;\n        PInvokeSmokeTestPassed = failed == 0;\n        PInvokeSmokeTestDetail = string.Join(\"; \", outcomes);\n        StatusText = failed == 0\n            ? $\"P/Invoke smoke: {total} of {total} probes answered.\"\n            : $\"P/Invoke smoke FAILED: {failed} of {total} probes did not answer.\";\n\n        Log($\"P/Invoke smoke ({(failed == 0 ? \"PASS\" : \"FAIL\")}): {string.Join(\"; \", outcomes)}\");\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>\n    /// Whether the last <see cref=\"RunPInvokeSmokeTestCommand\"/> run passed; null before it has run.\n    /// Exposed so the automation report and the E2E scenarios read the SAME value the user sees rather\n    /// than re-deriving it.\n    /// </summary>\n    public bool? LoadImageFromPathAsync(string path, string sourceLabel)\n    {\n        // GUI-C-186f: asked here, which is also where a file dialog's answer arrives (the dialog is modal and may outlive the moment the\n        // command was accepted), so a shutdown that began while it was open refuses the load.\n        if (RefusedWhileTransitioning(\"Load image\"))\n        {\n            return;\n        }\n\n        Settings.LastRawDirectory = Path.GetDirectoryName(path) ?? string.Empty;\n        _openGeneration++;   // GUI-C-236c: a timing that began before this open must not be written after it\n        _openStartedAt = System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch.GetTimestamp();   // GUI-C-236b (U8): the open starts reading\n        var loadedFrame = _backend.LoadRawImage(path, Settings);\n        _openReadEndedAt = System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch.GetTimestamp();\n        ActiveImageSourcePath = path;   // GUI-C-232b: only after the load SUCCEEDED, so a failed open never renames the image that is still open\n        DrainBackendTelemetry();\n\n        // GUI-C-233g: a new frame ends whatever render stood (one call; the record and everything derived from it go with it)\n        _sourceFrame = loadedFrame;\n        SourceImage = loadedFrame.Preview;\n        InvalidateRender(staleReason: null);\n        ActiveImageFrame = loadedFrame;\n        RefreshCorrectedAvailability();\n        ResetComparisonView();\n        ActiveImageSummary = loadedFrame.Summary;\n        MetadataText = loadedFrame.MetadataText;\n        StatusText = $\"Loaded {sourceLabel} '{path}'.\";\n        Log($\"Loaded {sourceLabel} '{path}'.\");\n        RememberRecentRawFile(path);\n        await ApplyDisplayPipelineAsync();\n    }\n\n    // @MX:NOTE: [AUTO] Display pipeline runs on Task.Run (thread pool); await resumes on dispatcher thread, so ObservableCollection writes are safe\n    private async Task ApplyDisplayPipelineAsync()\n    {\n        if (RefusedWhileTransitioning(\"Display pipeline\"))\n        {\n            return;\n        }\n\n        // GUI-C-190: an Apply takes a new request number too, so a result that arrives after a NEWER Apply started is dropped.\n        var ticket = TakeRequestTicket();\n        var backend = (IXpeBackend)ticket.Backend!;\n\n        if (ActiveImageFrame is null)\n        {\n            StatusText = \"Display pipeline requires a loaded raw image.\";\n            Log(StatusText);\n            RaiseAlert(new AlertEntry\n            {\n                Severity = \"WARN\",\n                Code = \"DISPLAY_NO_IMAGE\",\n                Message = StatusText,\n                Timestamp = DateTimeOffset.Now\n            });\n            return;\n        }\n\n        // GUI-C-236b (U8): the first display pipeline after an open is the one whose picture ends the timed span\n        var timedOpenStartedAt = _openStartedAt;\n        var timedReadEndedAt = _openReadEndedAt;\n        var timedGeneration = _openGeneration;\n        _openStartedAt = 0;\n        var applyStartedAt = System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch.GetTimestamp();\n\n        CancellationTokenSource? cancellationMarker = null;\n        StatusText = \"Applying display pipeline...\";\n        Log($\"Display pipeline requested: mode={Settings.VoiLutMode}, bodyPart={Settings.SelectedBodyPart}, center={Settings.VoiWindowCenter}, width={Settings.VoiWindowWidth}, GSDF={Settings.GsdfEnabled}, calibrationEval=[{CalibrationEvaluationSummary}].\");\n\n        try\n        {\n            var sourceFrame = ActiveImageFrame;\n            var inputs = Settings.Snapshot();\n            // #180 (GUI-C-103): where the time to a drawn frame goes. `work` covers the background\n            // task (chain + display); `total` covers this method, so the difference is the UI-thread\n            // share. Neither covers the render itself \u2014 that is measured from outside, by the E2E.\n            var total = System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch.StartNew();\n            var work = System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch.StartNew();\n            // #225 (GUI-C-154, row 11): one cancellation source per render, replaced rather than\n            // reused so a stop can only ever affect the render it was pressed during.\n            var cancellation = new CancellationTokenSource();\n            _renderCancellation?.Dispose();\n            _renderCancellation = cancellation;\n            cancellationMarker = cancellation;\n            // Measured (GUI-C-154): without clearing this when the render ENDS, Stop answered\n            // \"the render in flight will be discarded\" on a render that had finished seconds earlier \u2014\n            // the source stayed non-null, so the no-op path never ran. The marker is cleared in the\n            // finally below, and only when it is still this render's own source.\n\n            // #180 (GUI-C-99): the chain runs first, on the same snapshot as the display (#171 \u2461), and the\n            // display starts from the chain's last result \u2014 the raw frame only when no stage produced pixels.\n            var (chain, processedFrame) = await Task.Run(() =>\n            {\n                var chainResult = backend.RunChain(sourceFrame, ProcessingChainPlan.BuildStages(inputs), inputs);\n                return (chainResult, backend.ApplyDisplayPipeline(sourceFrame, chainResult, inputs));\n            });\n            var workMs = work.Elapsed.TotalMilliseconds;\n            var workEndedAt = System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch.GetTimestamp();\n\n            // GUI-C-186f: a shutdown or a replacement may have started while the chain waited (for the AI gate, for instance). Its\n            // result belongs to a backend that is going away: nothing on screen changes, and no Lane B work is scheduled.\n            if (!IsCurrent(ticket))\n            {\n                Log($\"Display pipeline result dropped after {workMs:0} ms: {WhyStale(ticket)}\");\n                return;\n            }\n\n            // The native calls above are synchronous and ran to completion; what cancellation decides is\n            // whether their result is APPLIED. Discarding it here keeps the viewport and the status\n            // describing the frame that is actually on screen.\n            if (cancellation.IsCancellationRequested)\n            {\n                StoppedRenderCount++;\n                PreviewStaleReason = StalePipelineFailed;\n                StatusText = $\"Render stopped; the result was discarded after {workMs:0} ms of work.\";\n                Log($\"Display pipeline stopped by the user after {workMs:0} ms; result discarded.\");\n                DrainBackendTelemetry();\n                return;\n            }\n\n            DrainBackendTelemetry();\n            var renderBackend = RenderBackend.From(backend.GetRuntimeInfo());\n            var chainReport = ReportChain(chain, renderBackend.Mode == \"Native\");\n\n            // GUI-C-232b: the save candidate is committed together with the render and only from THIS (current, not cancelled) result; a run that applied no preprocess clears it.\n            _committedCorrected = (backend as ICorrectedImageSource)?.CorrectedFor(chain);\n            ActiveImageFrame = processedFrame;\n            RefreshCorrectedAvailability();\n            ProcessedImage = processedFrame.ProcessedPreview ?? processedFrame.Preview;\n            if (timedOpenStartedAt != 0)\n            {\n                // GUI-C-236b (U8): the picture is handed to the viewport; the end of the timed span is two composition ticks later (not awaited here: nothing below waits for it)\n                _ = PublishFrameTimingAsync(timedGeneration, ProcessedImage!, timedOpenStartedAt, timedReadEndedAt, applyStartedAt, workEndedAt, System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch.GetTimestamp(), chain.Timings);\n            }\n\n            PreviewStaleReason = null;   // #171 \u2462: this render is current; \u2460 is re-evaluated just below\n            // GUI-C-233g: the commit. One record, made from this render's own inputs, chain, window, summary and the backend that ran it (asked from the ticket's backend, not from whatever is current later).\n            var committed = new RenderRecord(\n                inputs,\n                renderBackend,\n                RenderedVoi.From(inputs, processedFrame.AppliedVoi),\n                chain,\n                chainReport.Status,\n                chainReport.AiLabel,\n                chainReport.PreprocessRan,\n                chainReport.PreprocessStages,\n                processedFrame.DisplayPipelineSummary,\n                Timings: string.Empty,\n                Id: ++_renderSequence);\n            SetRender(committed);\n            MetadataText = processedFrame.MetadataText;\n            ActiveImageSummary = processedFrame.DisplayPipelineApplied\n                ? $\"{processedFrame.Summary} | {processedFrame.DisplayPipelineSummary}\"\n                : processedFrame.Summary;\n            StatusText = $\"{chain.Summary} | {processedFrame.DisplayPipelineSummary} | {ExposureIndexText}\";\n            await RenderLanesAsync(sourceFrame, inputs, ProcessedImage, ticket, committed.Id);\n            if (!IsCurrent(ticket))\n            {\n                return; // the lanes' wait outlived the backend: the timing line below would describe a render that was dropped\n            }\n\n            // GUI-C-191: the Candidate lane's chain runs the AI stage too (it is the same chain with the lane's overrides), so it is a\n            // SECOND call into the AI session for one Apply, and it ends after the status read ReportChain asked for. A worker switched\n            // off by that call showed nothing until the next Apply. Asked again here, after the lanes: the read is coalesced, so an\n            // Apply whose lanes made no AI call costs one more read of a state that did not change.\n            RefreshAiWorkerStatus();\n\n            // The timings exist only after the lanes finished; they are added to THIS render's record, and only if it is still the one on screen (a newer render or an invalidation wins).\n            var timings = string.Join(\"; \", new[]\n            {\n                $\"work={workMs:0} ms\",\n                $\"vm={total.Elapsed.TotalMilliseconds - workMs:0} ms\",\n                processedFrame.DisplayTimings,\n            }.Where(part => !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(part)));\n            UpdateRender(committed.Id, r => r with { Timings = timings });\n\n            OnPropertyChanged(nameof(FaultInjectionStatus));\n        }\n        catch (Exception ex)\n        {\n            if (!IsCurrent(ticket))\n            {\n                Log($\"Display pipeline of a backend that is no longer current failed ({ex.Message}); dropped.\");\n                return;\n            }\n\n            OnPropertyChanged(nameof(FaultInjectionStatus));\n            PreviewStaleReason = StalePipelineFailed;   // #171 \u2462\n            StatusText = $\"Display pipeline failed: {ex.Message}\";\n            Log(StatusText);\n            RaiseAlert(new AlertEntry\n            {\n                Severity = \"ERROR\",\n                Code = \"DISPLAY_PIPELINE_FAILED\",\n                Message = ex.Message,\n                Timestamp = DateTimeOffset.Now\n            });\n        }\n        finally\n        {\n            if (ReferenceEquals(_renderCancellation, cancellationMarker))\n            {\n                _renderCancellation = null;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>\n    /// The preset the active backend last produced, kept so a caller can check that it was applied\n    /// without knowing which backend produced it. #135: the automation harness used to compare the\n    /// settings against MockXpeBackend's literal values, which made the check fail under the real\n    /// DLL \u2014 whose abdomen window (C=40/W=400, HU) is the clinically validated one.\n    /// </summary>\n    public VoiPreset? The measurements line carries the\n        // longest gap between two checks (maxUiGapMs), which is that stall.\n        var measured = 0;\n        _aiFreshnessTimer = new System.Windows.Threading.DispatcherTimer(\n            TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1), System.Windows.Threading.DispatcherPriority.Background,\n            (_, _) =>\n            {\n                refresher.CheckFreshness();\n                if (refresher.MeasurementsVersion != measured)\n                {\n                    measured = refresher.MeasurementsVersion;\n                    OnPropertyChanged(nameof(AiWorkerDiagnostics));   // GUI-C-192d: the native CI log reads the measurements from there\n                }\n            },\n            _uiDispatcher);\n        _aiFreshnessTimer.Start();\n        return refresher;\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>Runs on a background thread, for the backend that was current when the read was requested.</summary>\n    private static AiWorkerStatus? Raise the generation and show Unknown before anything is awaited, so a\n        // status read that was started under the old session (a \"switched off\" answer above all) cannot be applied to the new one. The restart\n        // used to leave the generation alone, and the same backend with the same generation made the old answer look current.\n        AiStatus.Reset();\n        try\n        {\n            var directory = Settings.AiModelDirectory;\n            var result = await Task.Run(() => session.RestartAiSession(directory));\n            if (!IsCurrent(ticket))\n            {\n                Log(\"AI session restart finished for a backend that is no longer current; its result was dropped.\");\n                return;\n            }\n\n            DrainBackendTelemetry();\n            StatusText = result.Message;\n            Log(result.Message);\n        }\n        catch (Exception ex)\n        {\n            if (!IsCurrent(ticket))\n            {\n                Log($\"AI session restart of a backend that is no longer current failed ({ex.Message}); dropped.\");\n                return;\n            }\n\n            StatusText = $\"AI session could not be restarted: {ex.Message}\";\n            Log(StatusText);\n        }\n\n        RefreshAiWorkerStatus();\n    }\n\n\n    /// <summary>The pixel chain of the processed image on screen (#180, GUI-C-99), or null before the first render.</summary>\n    public ChainResult? The subscription to <c>CompositionTarget.Rendering</c> is taken\n    /// and released HERE and nowhere else, and it is released in a <c>finally</c>: whichever way the wait ends, no handler is left behind (a static event keeps every handler - and the closure it holds - alive).\n    /// WPF can raise <c>Rendering</c> more than once for one frame; a frame is told by its <c>RenderingTime</c>, so one frame counts once.\n    /// </summary>\n    internal static async Task<CompositionWait> WaitForCompositionTicksAsync(int ticks, TimeSpan limit, CancellationToken cancel)\n    {\n        var done = new TaskCompletionSource<CompositionWait>(TaskCreationOptions.RunContinuationsAsynchronously);\n        var seen = 0;\n        TimeSpan? lastFrame = null;\n        EventHandler handler = (_, e) =>\n        {\n            var frame = (e as System.Windows.Media.RenderingEventArgs)?.RenderingTime;\n            if (frame is not null && frame == lastFrame)\n            {\n                return;\n            }\n\n            lastFrame = frame;\n            if (++seen >= ticks)\n            {\n                done.TrySetResult(CompositionWait.Ticked);\n            }\n        };\n\n        using var timeout = new CancellationTokenSource(limit);\n        using var onTimeout = timeout.Token.Register(() => done.TrySetResult(CompositionWait.TimedOut));\n        using var onCancel = cancel.Register(() => done.TrySetResult(CompositionWait.Cancelled));\n        try\n        {\n            Interlocked.Increment(ref ActiveCompositionSubscriptions);\n            System.Windows.Media.CompositionTarget.Rendering += handler;\n            return await done.Task;\n        }\n        finally\n        {\n            System.Windows.Media.CompositionTarget.Rendering -= handler;\n            Interlocked.Decrement(ref ActiveCompositionSubscriptions);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>Called when the backend is going away (the window is closing): a wait still running ends as cancelled and writes nothing.</summary>\n    private void CancelFrameTiming()\n    {\n        var old = Interlocked.Exchange(ref _frameTimingLifetime, new CancellationTokenSource());\n        old.Cancel();\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>\n    /// Waits for the second composition tick after <paramref name=\"shown\"/> was handed to the viewport and writes the line - unless, when the wait ends, it no longer describes what is on screen: a newer\n    /// open began (<paramref name=\"generation\"/> is no longer the current one) or another picture replaced <paramref name=\"shown\"/>. Each is caught on its own so one missing library does not hide the state\n    /// of the others, and the outcome of every probe is written to the log rather than summarised away.\n    /// </summary>\n    private void RunPInvokeSmokeTest()\n    {\n        var outcomes = new List<string>();\n        var failed = 0;\n\n        // Probe 1: allocate and release a buffer through xpe_common. Chosen because it both crosses the\n        // ABI and returns something checkable \u2014 a code AND a non-null pointer.\n        try\n        {\n            var code = XpeCommonNative.xpe_alloc_image(16, 16, XpePixelFormatNative.UInt16, out var buffer);\n            if (code != 0)\n            {\n                failed++;\n                outcomes.Add($\"xpe_alloc_image -> code {code} (expected 0)\");\n            }\n            else if (buffer.Data == IntPtr.Zero)\n            {\n                failed++;\n                outcomes.Add(\"xpe_alloc_image -> code 0 but a null data pointer\");\n                XpeCommonNative.xpe_free_image(ref buffer);\n            }\n            else\n            {\n                var freeCode = XpeCommonNative.xpe_free_image(ref buffer);\n                if (freeCode != 0)\n                {\n                    failed++;\n                    outcomes.Add($\"xpe_free_image -> code {freeCode} (expected 0)\");\n                }\n                else\n                {\n                    outcomes.Add(\"xpe_alloc_image/xpe_free_image -> ok\");\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        catch (Exception ex)\n        {\n            failed++;\n            outcomes.Add($\"xpe_alloc_image threw {ex.GetType().Name}: {ex.Message}\");\n        }\n\n        // Probe 2: the display library answers with a version string, and it is not the mock's.\n        try\n        {\n            var version = XpeDisplayNative.GetVersion();\n            if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(version) || version == \"unknown\")\n            {\n                failed++;\n                outcomes.Add($\"xpe_display_version -> '{version}'\");\n            }\n            else\n            {\n                outcomes.Add($\"xpe_display_version -> '{version}'\");\n            }\n        }\n        catch (Exception ex)\n        {\n            failed++;\n            outcomes.Add($\"xpe_display_version threw {ex.GetType().Name}: {ex.Message}\");\n        }\n\n        // Probe 3: the alert queue answers. A negative count would mean the call crossed but the\n        // contract did not hold, which is a different failure from the library being absent.\n        try\n        {\n            var count = XpeCommonNative.xpe_get_pending_alert_count();\n            if (count < 0)\n            {\n                failed++;\n                outcomes.Add($\"xpe_get_pending_alert_count -> {count} (expected >= 0)\");\n            }\n            else\n            {\n                outcomes.Add($\"xpe_get_pending_alert_count -> {count}\");\n            }\n        }\n        catch (Exception ex)\n        {\n            failed++;\n            outcomes.Add($\"xpe_get_pending_alert_count threw {ex.GetType().Name}: {ex.Message}\");\n        }\n\n        var total = outcomes.Count;\n        PInvokeSmokeTestPassed = failed == 0;\n        PInvokeSmokeTestDetail = string.Join(\"; \", outcomes);\n        StatusText = failed == 0\n            ? $\"P/Invoke smoke: {total} of {total} probes answered.\"\n            : $\"P/Invoke smoke FAILED: {failed} of {total} probes did not answer.\";\n\n        Log($\"P/Invoke smoke ({(failed == 0 ? \"PASS\" : \"FAIL\")}): {string.Join(\"; \", outcomes)}\");\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>\n    /// Whether the last <see cref=\"RunPInvokeSmokeTestCommand\"/> run passed; null before it has run.\n    /// Exposed so the automation report and the E2E scenarios read the SAME value the user sees rather\n    /// than re-deriving it.\n    /// </summary>\n    public bool? this build is not running from a checkout.\";\n                Log($\"Benchmark runner not run: {ex.Message}\");\n                return;\n            }\n\n            var plan = BenchmarkRunnerService.Resolve(repositoryRoot);\n            if (!plan.IsReady)\n            {\n                StatusText = plan.Message;\n                Log(plan.Message);\n                return;\n            }\n\n            if (App.IsAutomationMode)\n            {\n                BenchmarkLaunchSuppressed = true;\n                StatusText = $\"{plan.Message} (launch suppressed under automation)\";\n                Log(StatusText);\n                return;\n            }\n\n            var verdict = await ExecuteRunnerAsync(\"Benchmark runner\", \"ctest\", plan.Arguments,\n                repositoryRoot, BenchmarkRunnerService.Summarize);\n            if (verdict.HasValue)\n            {\n                BenchmarkPassed = verdict;\n            }\n        }\n        finally\n        {\n            BenchmarkRunning = false;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>\n    /// Resolves a console runner, runs it off the UI thread, and writes the verdict to the status bar.\n    /// Returns the verdict, or null when the runner could not be reached at all (no checkout, not built)\n    /// \u2014 that is \"did not run\", which is not the same as a failure and must not be recorded as one.\n    /// </summary>\n    private async Task<bool?> RunConsoleRunnerAsync(\n        string label, string projectDirectory, string executableName, string? overridePath)\n    {\n        string exePath;\n        if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(overridePath))\n        {\n            // Command-line override (#225, GUI-C-159). It exists so the FAILING path can be observed:\n            // a scenario stages a copy of the runner outside the repository, where it genuinely dies,\n            // and points this at it. Without it a test could only ever watch the self-check succeed,\n            // which cannot separate \"reports success correctly\" from \"reports everything as success\".\n            exePath = overridePath!;\n        }\n        else\n        {\n            try\n            {\n                var repositoryRoot = GuiFixtureManifestService.FindRepositoryRoot(AppContext.BaseDirectory);\n                exePath = Path.Combine(\n                    repositoryRoot, \"gui\", projectDirectory, \"bin\", \"Debug\", \"net8.0-windows\",\n                    executableName);\n            }\n            catch (InvalidOperationException ex)\n            {\n                StatusText = $\"{label} needs the repository; this build is not running from a checkout.\";\n                Log($\"{label} not run: {ex.Message}\");\n                return null;\n            }\n        }\n\n        if (!File.Exists(exePath))\n        {\n            StatusText = $\"{label} runner is not built.\";\n            Log($\"{label} not run: '{exePath}' does not exist. Build gui/{projectDirectory} first.\");\n            return null;\n        }\n\n        return await ExecuteRunnerAsync(label, exePath, arguments: null, workingDirectory: null, summarize: null);\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>\n    /// The one place a runner process is started and its verdict written (#225 rows 15, 16 and 17). Rows 15 and\n    /// 16 reach it through <c>RunConsoleRunnerAsync</c>, which finds their executable; row 17 reaches it directly\n    /// because its executable is ctest, found on PATH, and what must exist is a build tree.\n    /// <paramref name=\"summarize\"/> picks the line the verdict quotes from stdout; null keeps the choice the\n    /// self-check and E2E runners were measured with (GUI-C-158).\n    ///\n    /// <para>Returns null when nothing could be started (the executable is missing, ctest is not on PATH, the file\n    /// is not a program), false when something ran and exited non-zero, true when it exited zero. The status line\n    /// says \"did not run\" for the first and \"FAILED (exit N)\" for the second (GUI-C-177).</para>\n    /// </summary>\n    private async Task<bool?> ExecuteRunnerAsync(\n        string label, string exePath, IReadOnlyList<string>? arguments, string? workingDirectory,\n        Func<string, string?>? summarize)\n    {\n        StatusText = $\"Running {label}\u2026\";\n        Log($\"{label} started: '{exePath}'.\");\n\n        try\n        {\n            var outcome = await Task.Run(() => RunnerProcess.Run(exePath, arguments, workingDirectory, summarize));\n\n            // The wording, and with it the difference between \"could not be started\" and \"ran and failed\", is\n            // RunnerProcess.Describe's: nothing here words an outcome. A start that failed has a null verdict,\n            // \"did not run\", which is not a failure and is not recorded as one (GUI-C-177).\n            StatusText = RunnerProcess.Describe(label, exePath, outcome, quotesSummary: summarize is not null);\n            Log(outcome.Started\n                ? $\"{label} finished: exit={outcome.ExitCode}, {outcome.ElapsedMs:0} ms, reported line: {outcome.LastLine}\"\n                : $\"{label} did not run: {outcome.StartError}\");\n            return outcome.Verdict;\n        }\n        catch (Exception ex)\n        {\n            // Reachable only AFTER the process started (RunnerProcess.Run returns a failed start as an outcome,\n            // not as an exception): something ran and its output could not be read. That is not \"did not run\".\n            StatusText = $\"{label} ended abnormally: {ex.Message}\";\n            Log($\"{label} ended abnormally: {ex.GetType().Name}: {ex.Message}\");\n            return false;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>True while the self-check child process is running.</summary>\n    public bool SelfCheckRunning\n    {\n        get => _selfCheckRunning;\n        private set => SetProperty(ref _selfCheckRunning, value);\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>Verdict of the last self-check run; null before one has finished.</summary>\n    public bool? The replacement itself takes no AI gate (the backends are not IDisposable and Initialize does not touch\n        // the session), so it stays synchronous; it just waits its turn.\n        if (RefusedWhileTransitioning(\"Initialize backend\"))\n        {\n            return;\n        }\n\n        // GUI-C-186f: everything started for the backend being replaced is stale from NOW (not from the moment the new one is\n        // attached): a task of the old backend that finishes during this method must already find its ticket out of date.\n        Lifecycle.Bump();\n\n        // GUI-C-186d: the status on screen belongs to the backend being replaced. One reason it might have had\n            // is real: alerts from the previous backend could be read as describing the new one. A\n            // separator satisfies that reading as well as the opposite one, so neither has to be proven.\n            //\n            // The drain cursors below are a different thing and are still reset: they are backend\n            // state \u2014 the new backend's queue starts at 0 and must be read from 0.\n            if (Logs.Count > 0 || Alerts.Count > 0)\n            {\n                Log(\"--- backend re-initialised ---\");\n            }\n\n            _drainedBackendLogCount = 0;\n            _drainedBackendAlertCount = 0;\n\n            lock (_telemetryLock)\n            {\n                (_backend as IDisposable)?.Dispose();\n                _backend = _backendFactory(Settings);\n            }\n\n            // GUI-C-233g (Codex #176): the picture on screen was produced by the backend that was just disposed.                        Timestamp = DateTimeOffset.Now,\n                    });\n            }\n\n            if (stage.Status == StageStatus.RequestedNotApplied)\n            {\n \"CHAIN_STAGE_NOT_APPLIED\",\n                    Message = $\"{stage.StageId} was requested and not applied; the display used its input. {stage.Reason}\",\n                    Timestamp = DateTimeOffset.Now,\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        return new ChainReport(status, aiLabel, preprocessRan, preprocessStages);\n    }\n\n    // @MX:WARN: [AUTO] async void; _drainedBackendLogCount = snapshot.LogTotal;\n\n            pendingAlerts = snapshot.Alerts.Where(alert => alert is not null).ToList();\n            _drainedBackendAlertCount = snapshot.AlertTotal;\n /// <see cref=\"ApiReferenceService\"/>, never taken from operator input, and existence is checked before\n    /// anything is launched.</para>\n    ///\n    /// <para>The three answers are all real and all different: not generated (with how to generate it),\n    /// generated part-way, opened (with when it was generated). Every failure path returns a reason instead of throwing:\n    /// the caller surfaces it as an alert, and a missing calibration set is an expected state.\n    /// </summary>\n    public static PreprocessRunResult Run(\n        ushort[] rawPixels,\n        int width,\n        int height,\n        string offsetDirectory,\n        string gainDirectory,\n        string defectDirectory,\n        string bodyPart,\n        float kVp,\n        float pixelPitchMm,\n        bool measureExposureIndex = false,\n        string offsetMode = \"Auto\", string gainMode = \"Auto\", string defectMode = \"Auto\")\n    {\n        var offset = Path.Combine(offsetDirectory, OffsetFile);\n        var gain = Path.Combine(gainDirectory, GainFile);\n        var defect = Path.Combine(defectDirectory, DefectFile);\n\n        var applyOffset = CalibrationStageSelection.ShouldLoad(offsetMode, File.Exists(offset));\n        var applyGain = CalibrationStageSelection.ShouldLoad(gainMode, File.Exists(gain));\n        var applyDefect = CalibrationStageSelection.ShouldLoad(defectMode, File.Exists(defect));\n        var selected = new[] { (offset, applyOffset), (gain, applyGain), (defect, applyDefect) };\n        var missing = selected.Where(p => p.Item2 && !File.Exists(p.Item1)).Select(p => p.Item1).ToArray();\n        if (missing.Length > 0)\n        {\n            // GUI-C-234b: a skip with a reason (<short>: <detail>), not a failure - The restart does not touch the epoch unless asked to, so the view model's own Restart AI wiring\n/// is what is observed; <see cref=\"ReplaceSessionWithoutTellingAnyone\"/> moves the epoch the way a frame's re-init would.\n/// </summary>\ninternal sealed class ReplacedSessionBackend : ScenarioBackend, IAiSessionBackend\n{\n    public bool HasAiSession => true;\n\n    public readonly ManualResetEventSlim OldReadEntered = new();\n    public readonly ManualResetEventSlim OldReadRelease = new();\n    private int _reads;\n    private int _epoch;\n\n    public AiWorkerStatus GetAiWorkerStatus()\n    {\n        if (Interlocked.Increment(ref _reads) == 1)\n        {\n            OldReadEntered.Set();\n            OldReadRelease.Wait(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30));\n            return new AiWorkerStatus(AiWorkerState.Disabled, 3, 3);\n        }\n\n        return new AiWorkerStatus(AiWorkerState.Active, 0, 3);\n    }\n\n    public AiRestartResult RestartAiSession(string modelDirectory) => new(true, \"AI session restarted: scripted\");\n\n    public void ReplaceSessionWithoutTellingAnyone() => Interlocked.Increment(ref _epoch);\n\n    int IAiSessionBackend.AiSessionEpoch => Volatile.Read(ref _epoch);\n}\n\n/// <summary>\n/// GUI-C-192f: an AI session whose status read answers from a script the scenario changes (Disabled first, then a failure), and whose epoch the\n/// scenario moves the way a frame's re-init does: with nobody calling Reset.\n/// </summary>\ninternal sealed class ScriptedSessionBackend : ScenarioBackend, IAiSessionBackend\n{\n    public bool HasAiSession => true;\n\n    public volatile bool ReadsFail;\n    private int _epoch;\n\n    public AiWorkerStatus GetAiWorkerStatus() =>\n        ReadsFail ?                          // A's held call ends, long after B finished\n            await Until(() => vm.Logs.Any(line => line.Contains(\"a newer Apply\", StringComparison.Ordinal)\n                || line.Contains(\"no longer current failed\", StringComparison.Ordinal)), \"A's late outcome to be recognised as stale\");\n            await FlushUi(); rows.Add(TableRow(\"same frame re-render, display fails\", vm));\n\n            // 2c. a NEW frame whose display fails: nothing of A survives\n            var secondFrame = Path.Combine(directory, XCal calibration fixture generator (QA-A-36, #141 #120)\n *\n * The repository carries no XCal fixtures, and binaries are not committed. This\n * tool builds a complete offset/gain/defect set from synthetic frames so GUI,\n * E2E and CI can create one into a temporary directory at run time.\n *\n * Usage:\n *   xpe_calib_fixture_gen --out <dir> [--width 1024] [--height 1024]\n *                         [--seed 0] [--expiry-ms 0]\n *\n *   --out         destination directory (must exist or be creatable)\n *   --width/-h    frame size in pixels (default 1024 x 1024)\n *   --seed        PRNG seed for the synthetic noise (default 0)\n *   --expiry-ms   expiry timestamp written into each file, Unix ms;\n *                 0 (default) means \"never expires\" (xcal_format.h 0x20)\n *   --gain-poly   also write gain_poly.xcal (XCAL_TYPE_GAIN_POLY); off by\n *                 default so the scalar set stays byte-identical (QA-A-136, #198)\n *   --poly-degree maximum fitted degree, 1-4 (default 2)\n *   --poly-levels dose levels to acquire, 3 or more (default 4)\n *   --caldata     QA-A-248 (#262): build the set from REAL calibration frames\n *                 instead of synthetic ones. <dir> holds dark.raw,\n *                 bright04.raw, bright05.raw, bright06.raw (uint16, headerless,\n *                 width x height) and BPMap.map (uint8 mask). The maps are made\n *                 the way QA-A-245 (test_zz_a241_measure.cpp,\n *                 A245_ExportAndAppPath) made calib-real-v2: offset from the one\n *                 dark frame (100 ms, 25 C), gain from the three flats with NO\n *                 dark reference (they are already offset-corrected, CalData_6\n *                 README), defect = BPMap.map as it is. --width/--height default\n *                 to 3072 in this mode. Not combinable with --gain-poly.\n *   --dark F, --bright F   QA-A-250: build the set from any number of REAL frames\n *                 (headerless little-endian uint16, width x height, offset-\n *                 UNcorrected: the dark pedestal is still in the bright frames).\n *                 Both options repeat. --dark-list L / --bright-list L read the\n *                 same from a text file, one path per line ('#' and empty lines\n *                 ignored, relative paths are relative to the list file).\n *   --gain-dark-ref mean|none|FILE   the dark reference the gain stage subtracts\n *                 from every bright frame: the rounded mean of the dark inputs\n *                 (default), none, or one raw file.\n *   --compare-bpm FILE   a defect map made by someone else (uint8 or uint16, any\n *                 non-zero value = defective). It is NOT used to make defect.xcal;\n *                 agreement with the generated map goes into manifest.json.\n *                 In this mode offset.xcal = mean of the dark inputs, gain.xcal =\n *                 the module's gain generator over the bright inputs, defect.xcal\n *                 = xpe_bpm_generate over both. Refusals (nothing is written):\n *                 fewer than 5 dark frames, fewer than 5 bright frames (gain) or\n *                 10 (defect map), a file that is missing or not width x height x 2\n *                 bytes, a frame with more than 0.1 % of its pixels at 65535, bright\n *                 frames for the gain map that span more than one dose (QA-A-250b,\n *                 QA-A-250c): the signal of a frame is formed exactly as the gain\n *                 generator forms it, the mean over the pixels of max(0, frame -\n *                 gain dark reference) (reference: --gain-dark-ref, none = 0); the\n *                 largest and the smallest signal differ by more than 1.25, or a\n *                 frame has no signal left (exit 12).\n *                 QA-A-250c: the same file twice in one role (same path, same file\n *                 by fs::equivalent, or same sha-256), exit 13.\n *                 QA-A-250d: --out must not exist or must be an EMPTY directory;\n *                 a non-empty --out is refused (exit 14, nothing is written):\n *                 there is no overwrite, a new set goes to a new folder. The set\n *                 is built in a directory of its own, <out>.building-<pid>-<ms>,\n *                 beside --out and published with ONE directory rename onto --out\n *                 once all four files exist. A refusal or a failure (exit 5-8)\n *                 leaves neither --out nor its own work directory, and a work\n *                 directory of another run is never touched.\n *   --bpm-bright F, --bpm-bright-list L   QA-A-250b: the bright frames of the DEFECT\n *                 map, when they are not the gain frames. The gain map needs one\n *                 dose (xpe_calib_generate_gain averages the frames); the defect\n *                 map may use frames of several doses. Without these options the\n *                 --bright frames serve both.\n *\n * Output: offset.xcal, gain.xcal, defect.xcal, manifest.json\n *         (+ gain_poly.xcal with --gain-poly)\n *\n * DETERMINISM. The same arguments produce byte-identical files. Two things make\n * that true and both are deliberate:\n *\n *  - The synthetic frames come from std::mt19937 seeded with --seed, never from\n *    a random_device or the clock.\n *  - `created_epoch_ms` is written as 0 rather than \"now\". A wall-clock stamp\n *    would change every run and byte-identity is the point of a fixture; the\n *    field is not load-bearing for any consumer (expiry is carried separately\n *    by --expiry-ms).\n *\n * The pixel data itself comes from the SHIPPED generators\n * (`xpe_calib_generate_offset`, `xpe_calib_generate_gain`, `xpe_bpm_generate`),\n * so a fixture exercises the same maths the product does. Those generators\n * write their own files with a wall-clock stamp, so this tool runs them into a\n * scratch file, reads the payload straight back out of it, and rewrites the\n * final artifact with the fixed header.\n *\n * The payload is read with a plain ifstream rather than through the module's\n * global calibration store: `g_calib` and `g_calib_mutex` are internal to the\n * DLL and not exported (measured -- LNK2001 on both). No new export is added.\n */\n\n#include \"xpe/preprocess_api.h\"\n#include \"xpe/common/xpe_types.h\"\n#include \"xpe/common/xpe_error.h\"\n#include \"xpe/preprocess/xcal_format.h\"\n#include \"xcal_writer.hpp\"\n#include \"defect_ext.hpp\"\n#include \"xpe_sha256.hpp\"\n\n#ifdef _WIN32\n#include <process.h>\n#define XPE_GETPID _getpid\n#else\n#include <unistd.h>\n#define XPE_GETPID getpid\n#endif\n\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <filesystem>\n#include <fstream>\n#include <random>\n#include <string>\n#include <utility>\n#include <vector>\n\nnamespace fs = std::filesystem;\n\nnamespace {\n\nstruct Options {\n    std::string outDir;\n    uint32_t    width{1024};\n    uint32_t    height{1024};\n    uint32_t    seed{0};\n    uint64_t    expiryMs{0};\n\n    // QA-A-136 (#198): also emit gain_poly.xcal (XCAL_TYPE_GAIN_POLY).\n    //\n    // Off by default so the existing three fixtures are byte-identical to what\n    // this tool produced before -- callers that only want the scalar set get\n    // exactly what they got yesterday. One data set; a panel whose dose steps are smaller than 25 % would pass mixed.\nconstexpr double kGainDoseRatioLimit  = 1.25;\n\nstruct InputFrame {\n    std::string           role;\n    std::string           path;\n    std::vector<uint16_t> px;\n    std::string           sha;\n    double                mean{0.0};\n};\n\nstd::string jsonText(const std::string& text) {\n    std::string out;\n    for (char c : text) {\n        if (c == '\"' || c == '\\\\') out.push_back('\\\\');\n        out.push_back(c);\n    }\n    return out;\n}\n\nstd::string fixed(double v, int digits) {\n    char buf[64];\n    std::snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, \"%.*f\", digits, v);\n    return buf;\n}\n\n/** One path per line; '#' and empty lines are skipped; a relative path is relative to the list file. */\nbool readList(const std::string& listPath, std::vector<std::string>* out) {\n    std::ifstream f(listPath);\n    if (!f) {\n        std::fprintf(stderr, \"cannot open list %s\\n\", listPath.c_str());\n        return false;\n    }\n    const fs::path base = fs::path(listPath).parent_path();\n    std::string line;\n    while (std::getline(f, line)) {\n        while (!line.empty() && (line.back() == '\\r' || line.back() == ' ' || line.back() == '\\t')) line.pop_back();\n        size_t b = 0;\n        while (b < line.size() && (line[b] == ' ' || line[b] == '\\t')) ++b;\n        line.erase(0, b);\n        if (line.empty() || line[0] == '#') continue;\n        const fs::path p(line);\n        out->push_back((p.is_absolute() ? p : base / p).generic_string());\n    }\n    return true;\n}\n\n/** Reads every frame, refusing a wrong size (readFrame16) and a saturated frame.
